question: to the Commission Catarina Martins (The Left) Subject:

On 7 June 2026, Lehbib Mohamed Abdelaziz, a commander of the Polisario Front, was killed by a Moroccan drone strike. This assassination, which took place in the context of a war that Morocco instigated but has never acknowledged, is exacerbating the situation in Western Sahara, with the Commission a complicit party. In October 2024, the Court of Justice annulled two agreements between the EU and Morocco on the grounds that Sahrawis had not given their consent. In spite of this, the Commission then produced a revised agreement in late 2025, having excluded a legitimate partner from the process and turned a blind eye to increasing repression. One of the victims of the Moroccan crackdown is Naâma Asfari, who has been in prison for 16 years following an unlawful trial. He is currently on hunger strike in an attempt to draw attention to the plight of Sahrawi political prisoners. All EU trade agreements contain strict human rights safeguard clauses which are legally binding on both parties. The violation of Sahrawis’ right to self-determination, the perpetration of violence, and the assassination of political and military leaders all constitute a flagrant violation of these fundamental principles, thereby further undermining the legitimacy of the EU-Morocco trade agreements. In the light of the foregoing: 1.
What steps will the Commission take in response to this drone strike and Morocco’s human rights violations?
Will the Commission trigger the suspension clauses of the trade agreement over a breach of international law?
How can the Commission justify maintaining an agreement that excludes a legitimate representative recognised by the Court of Justice?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.8.2026) The EU recalls that now is the time for dialogue and negotiations and that any military escalation runs counter to this effort and should be avoided. The EU continues to support fully the United Nations-led process, in line with UN Security Council resolution 2797(2025)1, and the efforts of the UN Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to advance a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution. The EU remains committed to upholding human rights and international law in all its external action. Article 2 of the EU-Morocco Association Agreement2 enshrines respect for democratic principles and human rights as the foundation of the EU-Morocco partnership. Regarding the Agreement in the form of an Exchange of Letters signed on 3 October 2025, this new agreement replaces the earlier arrangement concerning tariff preferences for products originating in Western Sahara. It applies provisionally pending completion of the procedures required for its conclusion by the EU. The agreement includes provisions reflecting the requirements set out by the Court of Justice of the European Union.
